findings.artist_symptom: The statusline says "632 decisions" and has said something like it for weeks. A number that never changes colour is wallpaper. Nothing ever tells me one of them has been waiting two months.
findings.current_state: decisions.py's docstring calls the 30-day gate "the whole point" — the difference between a loop that is OBSERVABLE and one that is CLOSED. statusline.py calls collect(with_ages=False) to stay subprocess-free, so it renders a count with no age information and can never escalate.
findings.proposed_scaffold: Cache the age pass (one `git log --name-only` run) to harness/state/ on write, and have the statusline read the cached max-age alongside the live count. Then the segment can go from yellow to red on an over-age item without paying a subprocess per prompt. One number that can change colour beats one number that cannot.

findings.title: There is no tool anywhere for recording that a HUMAN ruled — only that an AI decided
findings.artist_symptom: The agent can write down what it decided. I cannot write down what I decided, except by typing a CLI command against a board that does not contain the thing I am ruling on.
findings.current_state: synapse_decide stamps every entry `tags + ["ai_decision"]` (tracker.py:508) — it is an agent-decision recorder. The only human channel is `decisions.py --resolve KEY --reason ... --by human` (:299), a terminal command keyed to receipt/flywheel items. The panel, where the artist actually is, has no ruling input at all.
findings.proposed_scaffold: Add the symmetric half: a one-word ruling input in the panel that writes to the SAME resolved.json keys as the CLI. The artist sees the open call where they already are, types one word, and the ruling propagates because both surfaces share item_key(). That is the artist-friendly scaffold the brief asks for, and DEC-2's unification is its precondition.
